title: Academic Status by General Weighted Average
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Academic Status by GWA]
provenance: The table is a pasted raster image on the PDF page (verify_extraction.py found an extra 397x205 image on page 21 and extract_tables() returned nothing); no parser can read it, so the rows were transcribed by hand from the page image. Boundary note: 3.50 is inclusive at the top of OK (GWA <= 3.50) and exclusive at the bottom of Probationary (3.50 < GWA), so a GWA of exactly 3.50 is OK. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11. Rows, boundaries and conditions confirmed against printed page 20.
text:
The academic status of a student is determined by his General Weighted Average (GWA) and certain conditions, as follows.
A student with a GWA from 1.00 to 3.50 inclusive has an academic status of OK.
A student with a GWA above 3.50 and up to 4.50 inclusive is placed on Probationary status.
A student is placed Out of the Program under any of the following conditions: (a) a GWA above 4.50 and up to 5.00; (b) two consecutive years classified under Probationary status; or (c) while under Probationary status, the student failed for the third time any course stipulated in the first two years of his curriculum, including PE, NSTP and Values Education.
Original table (Academic Status | Condition/s):
| OK | 1.00 <= GWA <= 3.50 |
| Probationary | 3.50 < GWA <= 4.50 |
| Out of the Program | 4.50 < GWA <= 5.00, or two consecutive years Probationary, or third failure of a first-two-years course while Probationary |

title: Latin Honors GWA Requirements
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Latin Honors]
provenance: The table extracts as three columns with the GWA lower bound split from its operator, so a naive row-to-sentence conversion produces wrong boundaries; transcribed by hand. Operator note: Summa's lower bound is inclusive (1.00 <= GWA <= 1.25) while Magna and Cum Laude are exclusive (1.25 < GWA, 1.50 < GWA), so a GWA of exactly 1.25 is Summa Cum Laude and exactly 1.50 is Magna Cum Laude. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11. The three honors, their GWA ranges and the operator boundaries confirmed against printed page 26.
text:
The following Latin Honors apply to graduating students of baccalaureate programs, based on General Weighted Average (GWA).
A GWA from 1.00 to 1.25 inclusive qualifies for Summa Cum Laude.
A GWA above 1.25 and up to 1.50 inclusive qualifies for Magna Cum Laude.
A GWA above 1.50 and up to 1.75 inclusive qualifies for Cum Laude.
A student with a GWA of exactly 1.25 qualifies for Summa Cum Laude; exactly 1.50 qualifies for Magna Cum Laude; exactly 1.75 qualifies for Cum Laude.
Original table (Latin Honor | GWA):
| SUMMA CUM LAUDE | 1.00 <= GWA <= 1.25 |
| MAGNA CUM LAUDE | 1.25 < GWA <= 1.50 |
| CUM LAUDE | 1.50 < GWA <= 1.75 |

title: MCM Grading System: numeric grades, letter grades, and status codes
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Grading Scale]
provenance: The grade/descriptor table spans the printed page 16->17 break; the header row appears only on page 16, so the 22 rows on page 17 are unlabelled in isolation. Rows transcribed verbatim from the page image, column labels supplied from page 16. Confirmed against the printed pages on 2026-07-11: (1) The two diploma letter grades appear as -A and -B, minus before the letter, exactly as extracted; this is the handbook's printed form, not an extraction artifact, and both prose and table now render them that way. (2) '2.00 Meritorious' falls between '1.75 Good' and '2.25 Very Satisfactory' -- confirmed as printed; this is the Mapua scale and must not be reordered. (3) Rows B+, B and -B have an empty Baccalaureate cell (preserved as '(blank)'), read as 'not used in baccalaureate programs'; A+, A and -A use '-' for the same meaning. (4) The handbook prints '1.0'; the prose gives both '1.00' and '1.0' so either query form matches, and the preserved table keeps '1.0'. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11.
text:
In baccalaureate programs, a grade of 1.00 (printed as 1.0 in the handbook) is Excellent, 1.25 is Superior, 1.50 is Very Good, 1.75 is Good, 2.00 is Meritorious, 2.25 is Very Satisfactory, 2.50 is Satisfactory, 2.75 is Fairly Satisfactory, 3.00 is Passed, and 5.00 is Failed; none of these numerical grades apply to diploma programs. The handbook lists no grade between 3.00 and 5.00.
Diploma programs use letter grades instead. As printed in the handbook these are -A (Very Good) and -B (Very Satisfactory), with the minus sign written before the letter; the full set is A+ (Excellent), A (Superior), -A (Very Good), B+ (Good), B (Meritorious), and -B (Very Satisfactory). These letter grades do not apply to baccalaureate programs.
Several marks are shared across both program types: INC means Incomplete, FA means Absent, DRP means Dropped, P means Passed, C means Continuing, F means Failed, AUD means Audit, and NA means Not Applicable. IP indicates a course is In Progress and applies only to baccalaureate programs.

FLOW CHART IN HEARING
OF STUDENT CASES
• The Center for Student Activities and Discipline conducts 
preliminary investigation and evaluation to determine prima facie

Discipline who has jurisdiction only in cases where Student/s are

b. Cases with equivalent sanction of suspension 2220 days with or without community service

and Discipline (based on the complexity of the case)

• After hearing of the case, decision/recommednation will be
formulated for implementation/approval of the concerned office/s 
• Appeal of cases with equivalent penalty of suspension of less than 
20% of the prescribed class days for the school year with or 
without community service imposed by the Center for Student 
Activities and Discipline shall be filed with the Office of the

Flow Chart in Hearing of Student Cases

1. Complaint Received. Complaints shall be filed at the Center for Student Activities and
   Discipline (CSAD), which has jurisdiction only in cases where a student is the respondent.
2. Preliminary Investigation & Evaluation. The CSAD conducts a preliminary investigation and
   evaluation to determine prima facie evidence.
3. Categorize the Case. Cases are categorized into three types:
   a. Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 1-10 days, with or without
      community service.
   b. Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 11-20 days, with or without
      community service.
   c. Cases recommended for the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CDI), at the
      discretion of the CSAD, based on the complexity of the case.
4. Hearing Proper. All cases are heard with strict observance of due process.
5. Decision & Recommendation. After the hearing, a decision/recommendation is formulated
   for implementation or approval by the concerned office(s).
6. Appeal?
   - If an appeal is filed: for cases with an equivalent penalty of suspension of less than
     20% of the prescribed class days (with or without community service) imposed by the
     CSAD, the appeal is filed with the Office of the Principal. For cases handled by the
     CDI, and those with an equivalent sanction of non-readmission and/or expulsion, the
     appeal is filed with the Office of the Executive Vice President. The concerned office
     then issues its own Decision & Recommendation.
   - If no appeal is filed: the decision is implemented after 10 days.
7. End.

text:
PROMOTION AND RETENTION

For Grade 7–10 Learners

If a student achieves a final grade of at least 75 in all learning areas, the decision is promotion to the next grade level.

If a student does not meet expectations in not more than two learning areas, they must pass remedial classes for those failing learning areas to be promoted to the next grade level. Otherwise, the student is retained in the same grade level.

If a student does not meet expectations in three or more learning areas, the decision is retention in the same grade level.

If a student passes all learning areas in Junior High School, they earn a Junior High School Certificate and are promoted to Senior High School.

title: Page 42 (manual correction)
provenance: Manually corrected via the Review tab for page 42.
text:
For Grade 11–12 Learners

When a student achieves final grades of at least 75 in all learning areas in a semester, they can proceed to the next grade level.

When a student does not meet expectations in a prerequisite subject in a learning area, they must pass remedial classes for failed competencies in the subject before being allowed to enroll in the higher level subject.

When a student does not meet expectations in any subject or learning area at the end of the semester, they must pass remedial classes for failed competencies in the subjects or learning areas to be allowed to enroll in the next semester. Otherwise, the learner must retake the subjects failed.

When a student passes all learning areas in Senior High School, they earn a Senior High School Certificate.

Step 1: Start
The process begins when an incident is reported.

Step 2: Complaint Received
Complaints shall be filed at the Prefect of Discipline (POD), which has jurisdiction only in cases where students are the respondents.

Step 3: Preliminary Investigation & Evaluation
The POD conducts a preliminary investigation and evaluation to determine prima facie evidence.

Step 4: Categorize the Case
Cases are categorized into three groups:

Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 1–10 days with or without community service.

Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 22–20 days with or without community service.

Cases recommended for the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CDI), upon the discretion of the POD based on the complexity of the case.

Step 5: Hearing Proper
All cases will be heard with strict observance of due process.

Step 6: Decision & Recommendation
After hearing the case, a decision or recommendation will be formulated for implementation and approval by the concerned office or offices.

Step 7: Appeal Decision

If Appealed (Yes): The case is routed to the Concerned Office. Appeals for cases with an equivalent penalty of suspension of less than 20% of the prescribed class days for the school year (with or without community service) imposed by the POD shall be filed with the Office of the Principal. Cases handled by the CDI and those with an equivalent sanction of non-readmission and/or expulsion shall be filed with the Office of Executive Vice President. The office then formulates a final Decision & Recommendation.

If Not Appealed (No): Implementation takes effect after 10 days, as the decision becomes final and executory after 10 days.

Step 8: End
The process concludes.
